themes.name: Enhancement of Critical Thinking Skills
themes.definition: The integration of artificial intelligence tools in educational contexts to foster and improve students' critical thinking abilities, as reported across various disciplines and educational levels.
evidence: [AlYakin2024] This study investigates the efficiency of blending artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to support behavioral intention and critical thinking in higher education settings.
[Maya2024] Students reported significant improvement in critical thinking skills (Mean = 3.82, SD = 0.86)
[Hong2025c] Generative AI tools present new opportunities for enhancing critical thinking (CT) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing instruction.

themes.name: Integration of Generative AI Tools
themes.definition: The application of generative artificial intelligence technologies, such as ChatGPT, in educational settings to support various learning activities, including task development, feedback, and interactive learning.
evidence: [Kim2023] this study aims to develop and explore a Critical-PBLL framework utilizing ChatGPT and Google Bard.

[Browning2024] This innovative practice full paper describes an indepth analysis of the pedagogical implications of incorporating generative artificial intelligence (genAI) tools, specifically Chat-GPT, into a data science course
[Chen2025f] This qualitative study examines student experiences with Generative AI (Gen AI) in Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL) designs for foreign language teaching (FLT).

themes.name: Ethical Considerations and Academic Integrity
themes.definition: Concerns and discussions regarding the ethical use of AI in education, including issues of plagiarism, academic integrity, overreliance, and the need for responsible AI implementation.
evidence: [Kim2023] students also reported negative learning experiences: Overreliance on ChatGPT and Google Bard, leading to reduced discussions; initial learning anxiety due to unfamiliarity with prompt literacy and critical thinking-based tasks; and technical limitations associated with ChatGPT.
[Alexander2025] explores teaching academic integrity in the context of AI use and focusing on critical thinking, proper citation, and policy adherence.
[Fahmi2025] reliance on AI in ethics and skills education practices resulted in reduced interaction and thinking in student learning.

themes.name: Pedagogical Models and Frameworks
themes.definition: Specific instructional models or frameworks designed to integrate AI into educational practices, such as the PAIR model, TPACK framework, BOPPPS model, or other structured approaches.
evidence: [Maya2024] This study investigates the implementation of the PAIR (Problem, AI, Interaction, Reflection) model in undergraduate business courses
[Ravi2025] This paper explores the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in engineering education through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework.
[Han2025b] this study introduces generative artificial intelligence technologies and interactive teaching models, integrated with the BOPPPS instructional design framework.

themes.name: Development of Specific Skills
themes.definition: The improvement of particular competencies such as argumentation, writing, problem-solving, and reflective thinking through the use of AI tools in educational contexts.
evidence: [Han2026] Results indicate significant improvements in argumentation levels and decision-making abilities
[Hong2025c] Generative AI tools present new opportunities for enhancing critical thinking (CT) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing instruction.
[Che2025] ChatGPT provided personalized feedback, helping students navigate complex tasks and enhance critical thinking.

themes.name: Impact on Student Engagement and Learning Outcomes
themes.definition: The effects of AI integration on student engagement, participation, and overall educational outcomes, including academic performance, learning efficiency, and interaction.
evidence: [Malang2025] Results revealed an overall positive perception, with a high average weighted mean of 3.85, indicating that ChatGPT supports students in understanding complex concepts, improving writing and critical thinking skills, increasing engagement, and facilitating collaborative learning.

[Huang2024] the intelligent teaching model positively impacted both teacher-student interaction and student learning ability. The teacher speech ratio decreased from 80.26% to 62.53%, and the students’ autonomy and participation increased significantly
[Molina-Barrón2025] The research findings offer suggestions and considerations for creating activities utilizing artificial intelligence, such as ChatGPT, while identifying areas needing improvement.

themes.name: Challenges and Limitations
themes.definition: Issues and drawbacks associated with the use of AI in education, such as overreliance on tools, technical problems, inaccuracies, hallucinations, and reduced human interaction.
evidence: [Kim2023] students also reported negative learning experiences: Overreliance on ChatGPT and Google Bard, leading to reduced discussions; initial learning anxiety due to unfamiliarity with prompt literacy and critical thinking-based tasks; and technical limitations associated with ChatGPT.

[King2025] However, there are also significant drawbacks, including the possibility of over-reliance on the tools and the hindrance of critical thinking, which can lead students to accept incorrect AI-generated answers.
[Rachmat2025] Students perceived chatbots to be unreliable due to providing wrong answers, inaccurate code snippets, hallucinations, and plagiarised content.

data.meta_observations: Critical thinking is a dominant theme across most abstracts, closely tied to the integration of generative AI tools like ChatGPT. Studies frequently employ mixed-method approaches, though some have noted quality issues such as missing quantitative data. Ethical considerations and challenges are consistently addressed, highlighting a balanced view of AI's role in education.
data.grounding_notes: Evidence is limited to explicit statements in the abstracts; no inferences are made for missing elements. Some abstracts have quality notes indicating missing objectives, methods, or results, which may affect the depth of analysis. All article keys are from the provided closed set, and quotes are verbatim as per the abstracts.
